title: auth.user.updated payload
description:
Payload for `auth.user.updated`, published by Auth when the account record itself changes — as opposed to a membership, which has its own events.

Today there is exactly one such change: **accepting an invitation**, which sets the password, moves the account from `pending` to `active`, and marks the address verified because redeeming a link sent to it proves control of it. Auth has no other write path to a user's own fields; a name or an address cannot be edited anywhere in this service yet, so this event is currently the account becoming usable and nothing else.

**No credential material, ever.** `changed` names `password` as a fact — the account now has one — and the value is not here and never will be. The same rule as FR-10's for responses.

The envelope's `org_id` is the organisation the invitation was issued in, matching `auth.user.created`. The user is global (ADR-0016) and the event is scoped anyway, because a consumer scopes on the envelope and ADR-0018 forbids a null standing in for "everyone".

The file name is the routing key — `SchemaDiscovery` keys the catalog by it.

user_id.description: Platform-wide user identity, as a string.

org_id.description: The organisation this change was made in the context of.

changed.description: Names of the fields that changed, so a consumer can act on the ones it cares about without diffing a projection it may not keep. Names only — a value appears in this payload only if it has its own property below.

status.description: The account's status after the change. This is `users.status`, the global axis — **not** a membership's, which says whether one organisation's access is open and is carried by `auth.membership.*` instead. Confusing the two is how an administrator of one organisation ends up appearing to sign somebody out of another.

email_verified.description: Whether the address is verified after the change.
